title: unified-rollouts-probing-staged-shadow-autorollback-enhancements
author: Priya Shah
description: Implements enhancements to the Unified Rollouts engine to support probing-based staged shadow canary deployments and more robust automated rollback workflows. Motivation: customers are running multi-tenant inference with mixed workloads and need a rollout strategy that probes new model variants under shadow and small live canary traffic with multi-metric checks before increasing traffic. This PR adds: 1) a probing scheduler that runs low-volume shadow probes to collect targeted metrics (latency P95, token-error-rate, model-quality delta) prior to canary ramp, 2) staged shadow -> canary transition logic that automatically promotes safe probes, 3) a composite metric matcher that evaluates multiple metrics with configurable weighting and thresholds, 4) stability guards and cooldown windows to reduce noisy auto-rollbacks, 5) enhanced observability hooks (trace spans, per-rollout metric breakdowns, and canary-probe dashboards), 6) additional e2e tests and simulation harnesses for deterministic autorollback scenarios. Backwards compatibility: the rollout config schema is backwards-compatible; new fields are optional and default to conservative behavior (no probing, existing canary semantics). Rollout operator defaults preserve current SLOs. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3241) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e deterministic autorollback scenarios - [x] dashboards and alert rules updated - [x] staged rollout migration script included - [x] docs + examples updated in redwood-docs Notes: this change centralizes probing logic in rollout-controller and adds a lightweight probe-worker for shadow traffic sampling. The probe worker is batchable and respects tenant isolation. See linked linear tickets for rollout plan and migration steps. Deployment plan: staged rollout to canary fleet for 2 weeks, initial probes at 0.1% traffic, promote only after 3 successful probe windows, rollback triggered only when composite_score exceeds configured failure threshold or if a single critical metric regresses beyond critical cutoff.
